title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is classifying the boundary strata of the compactified moduli stack \bar M_{g,ν}. Each stratum is indexed by a stable dual graph, which he calls an 'MD-graph'. Each vertex α carries a genus g_α, an 'order' μ̃_α (the number of edge half-edges at α) and a 'marked weight' (the number of legs). Each vertex has a 'type' (g_α, ν̂_α), where ν̂_α = μ̃_α + number of legs counts its special points. The 'modular multiplicity' \hat M_G is the product of the M_{g_α, ν̂_α}, taken modulo the action of Γ = Aut(G). Its 'modular dimension' is the sum of the vertex dimensions 3g_α − 3 + ν̂_α.

Part 1 (end of section II). For the three 1-dimensional strata found on p.57, he lists the automorphism data. The ambient spaces are \bar M_{0,5} and \bar M_{1,2}.
(i) Vertex α_0 of type (0,4) with 3 legs, joined to a (0,3) vertex with 2 legs. Here Γ = S_3 × S_2 (the legs are permuted among themselves). Γ^! = 1, the automorphisms of the graph with labelled legs. The image in S_{Î_{α_0}} ≅ S_4 (permutations of the 4 special points of α_0) is S_3, since the node branch is fixed.
(ii) A genus-0 vertex with a loop and 2 legs. Here Γ ≅ S_2 × S_2 (swap the legs; flip the loop) and Γ^! ≅ S_2 (the loop flip). Γ injects into S_4, with image S_2 × S_2.
(iii) A genus-1 vertex α_0 of type (1,1), joined to a (0,3) vertex with 2 legs. Here Γ ≅ S_2 and Γ^! = 1. The image in S_{Î_{α_0}} = S_1 is trivial; he crossed this out. This matches p.57: the action is trivial when g_{α_0} = 1.

Part 2 (section III, modular dimension 2). Since the vertex dimensions add up, a 2-dimensional modular multiplicity arises in two ways.
1°) All vertices but one are of type (0,3) and one vertex α_0 has type (0,5) or (1,2). For (0,5) the order is μ̃ ≤ 5 and the marked weight is 5 − μ̃. For (1,2) the order is μ̃ ∈ {1,2} and the marked weight is 2 − μ̃ ∈ {1,0}. Margin: 'hence two cases in reality'.
2°) All vertices but exactly two, α_0 and α_1, are of type (0,3). Each of α_0 and α_1 is of type (0,4) or (1,1). Margin: three cases, namely (0,4)+(0,4), (0,4)+(1,1), (1,1)+(1,1).

The next page lists the resulting models \hat M^!_{0,5}, \hat M^!_{1,2}, \hat M^!_{0,4}×\hat M^!_{0,4}, \hat M^!_{0,4}×\hat M^!_{1,1} and \hat M^!_{1,1}×\hat M^!_{1,1}. For each it gives the Γ-action through permutation groups of special points (e.g. via the wreath product Z/2 ⋉ (S_4 × S_4)). It concludes that the 'elementary' cases (0,4), (1,1), (0,5), (1,2) should hold the key to the discrete fundamental groups in general.

Purpose: reduce the local structure at infinity to a small number of elementary moduli spaces of dimension ≤ 2. This is the combinatorial groundwork of the 'two-level principle' of the Esquisse.
errors: Notational slip: '(α_i, μ̂_i)' should read (g_i, ν̂_i), i.e. genus and number of special points, as used elsewhere.
The bound μ̃ ≤ 5 (and μ̃ ≤ 3) implicitly assumes μ̃ ≥ 1, i.e. that the graph is not a single vertex. This is fine within the context (positive codimension) but is not stated.
Otherwise the automorphism groups and the case enumeration are correct: S_3×S_2 / 1 / S_3; S_2×S_2 / S_2 / S_2×S_2; S_2 / 1 / trivial.

ideas.what: Boundary strata of \bar M_{g,n} indexed by stable dual graphs. Each stratum is the product of the vertex moduli spaces modulo graph automorphisms, with the automorphisms acting through permutations of the special points.
ideas.modern_name: Stratification of the Deligne–Mumford–Knudsen compactification by stable graphs
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne–Mumford (1969), Knudsen (1983); standard in later work (e.g. Arbarello–Cornalba–Griffiths)
ideas.where_published: Implicit in Esquisse d'un programme (1984) via the 'Teichmüller tower'

ideas.what: Distinction between Γ (automorphisms with unlabelled legs) and Γ^! (automorphisms fixing the legs), and the image of Γ in S_{Î_{α_0}}
ideas.modern_name: Automorphism group of a stable graph vs. automorphisms fixing legs; the action on the vertex moduli spaces

ideas.what: Classification of strata of modular dimension ≤ 2: elementary building blocks M_{0,4}, M_{1,1} (dim 1) and M_{0,5}, M_{1,2} (dim 2)
ideas.modern_name: Two-level principle / Teichmüller tower generated by levels 1 and 2
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse d'un programme); developed by Lochak–Schneps, Ihara, Nakamura, Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), section on the Teichmüller tower

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine combinatorial enumeration of low-dimensional boundary strata and their automorphism groups. It is correct and fits the known genesis of the two-level principle published in the Esquisse. Nothing here is absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: In 2°, the image reads 'sont de genre 0, et de poids total 3 (i.e. d'ordre 1≤μ̃_α≤3 ...'. The '1≤μ̃_α≤3' is written in the left margin at the start of the line.
The '≃ S_2×S_2' under the second line of (f3) is attached with '||' to 'Im(Γ→S_4) ≃ Γ'.
In the third line of (f3), the crossed-out text after 'Γ^!≃1' presumably concerned the (trivial) image in S_{Î_{α_0}}. Below the graph it is written 'g_{α_0}=1'.
Margin of 2° in full: 'cela fait donc trois cas, suivant que les deux types sont deux (0,4), ou (0,4) et (1,1), ou deux (1,1)'.
